questions.question: A sound wave travels at 340 m/s with a frequency of 170 Hz. What is its wavelength in meters?
At 0°C the speed of sound in air is 332 m/s. What minimum distance in meters from a reflecting wall is required to hear a distinct echo? (Persistence of hearing = 0.1 s)
questions.explanation: Minimum echo distance d = (v × t) / 2 = (332 × 0.1) / 2 = 16.6 m.

questions.question: A convex lens has a focal length of +50 cm. What is its power in diopters?
An object placed 20 cm in front of a concave mirror produces a real inverted image at 20 cm. What is the focal length of the mirror in cm? (Give numerical magnitude)
questions.explanation: When u = v = 20 cm, the object is at center of curvature (r = 20 cm). Focal length f = r / 2 = 10 cm.

questions.question: Light travels from vacuum (c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s) into a medium where its speed is 1.5 × 10⁸ m/s. What is the refractive index of this medium?
Which optical property of light remains strictly invariant when a monochromatic light ray refracts from air into glass?
questions.explanation: Frequency depends exclusively on the emitting source oscillating mechanism and does not change across material interfaces, whereas speed and wavelength decrease.

questions.question: A patient cannot focus distant objects because their eyeball is elongated. What single type of lens corrects this condition?
questions.explanation: In myopia caused by an elongated eyeball, rays focus in front of the retina. A diverging (concave) lens spreads the rays slightly before entering the eye.

questions.question: A sonar operator receives an echo pulse 3 seconds after transmission. If acoustic velocity in sea water is 1500 m/s, what is the target depth in meters?
What phenomenon occurs when the angle of incidence in a denser medium exceeds the critical angle?
questions.explanation: When light reaches a rarer medium boundary at an incident angle greater than the critical angle, all light reflects back into the denser medium by total internal reflection.

questions.question: If an object is placed exactly at the principal focus of a convex lens, at what location will the image be formed?
questions.explanation: Rays originating from the focal point of a convex lens emerge parallel after refraction, intersecting only at infinity.

questions.question: A wave traveling along a stretched rope has an amplitude of 0.05 m, a frequency of 50 Hz, and a speed of 20 m/s. What is the distance between a crest and the adjacent trough?
questions.explanation: λ = v / f = 20 / 50 = 0.4 m. The distance between an adjacent crest and trough is half a wavelength: λ / 2 = 0.4 / 2 = 0.2 m.

questions.question: A sound wave of frequency 512 Hz travels in iron at 5120 m/s. How far does the wave travel in the time the source makes 100 complete vibrations?
questions.explanation: Time for 1 vibration T = 1/512 s. For 100 vibrations t = 100/512 s. Distance d = v × t = 5120 × (100 / 512) = 1000 m.

questions.question: An object 5 cm high is positioned 15 cm in front of a concave mirror with a radius of curvature of 20 cm. What is the height of the image formed?
options: -10 cm
+10 cm
-5 cm

questions.question: A ray of light traveling in air strikes an equilateral glass prism (apex angle A = 60°) symmetrically at an angle of minimum deviation of 30°. What is the refractive index of the prism material?
A converging lens of focal length 12 cm produces an erect image three times the size of the object. What is the object distance?
options: -8 cm
-16 cm
-4 cm
-24 cm
questions.explanation: For an erect image in a lens, m = +3 = v/u → v = 3u. 1/f = 1/v - 1/u → 1/12 = 1/(3u) - 1/u = -2/(3u) → 3u = -24 → u = -8 cm.

questions.question: A coin rests at the bottom of a glass container filled with liquid of refractive index 1.6 to a depth of 8 cm. By how much does the coin appear raised?
options: 3.0 cm
5.0 cm
2.0 cm
1.6 cm
questions.explanation: Apparent depth = real depth / n = 8 cm / 1.6 = 5 cm. Apparent upward shift = real depth - apparent depth = 8 - 5 = 3 cm.

questions.question: A student standing at a distance d from a cliff shouts. After hearing the echo, he steps back 85 m and shouts again, hearing the second echo 0.5 s after the first. What is the speed of sound?
questions.explanation: The extra round-trip distance is 2 × 85 m = 170 m. Time delay Δt = 0.5 s. Speed of sound v = 2Δd / Δt = 170 m / 0.5 s = 340 m/s.

questions.question: Two thin convex lenses with focal lengths 20 cm and 30 cm are placed in optical contact. What is the power of the combination?
A convex mirror with focal length 20 cm forms an image that is 1/4 the size of the object. Where is the object located?
options: 60 cm in front of mirror
80 cm in front of mirror
40 cm in front of mirror
20 cm in front of mirror
questions.explanation: For convex mirror, m = +1/4 = -v/u → v = -u/4. Mirror formula: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u → 1/20 = -4/u + 1/u = -3/u → u = -60 cm.

questions.question: Light takes 2.0 × 10⁻⁸ seconds to pass normally through a transparent glass slab of thickness 4.0 meters. What is the refractive index of this glass? (c = 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s)
questions.explanation: Speed in glass v = distance / time = 4.0 m / (2.0 × 10⁻⁸ s) = 2.0 × 10⁸ m/s. Refractive index n = c / v = 3.0 × 10⁸ / 2.0 × 10⁸ = 1.5.

questions.question: A person with presbyopia cannot read print closer than 50 cm. What spectacle lens power is needed to restore normal reading at 25 cm?
In a ripple tank, water waves have crests separated by 4 cm and travel at 24 cm/s. What is the frequency of the paddle vibrator?
options: 6 Hz
96 Hz
12 Hz
questions.explanation: f = v / λ = 24 cm/s ÷ 4 cm = 6 Hz.

questions.question: A sound source emits waves with wavelength 0.85 m into air where temperature is such that sound speed is 340 m/s. What is the period of this sound wave?
A microscope objective lens has a focal length of 10 mm. If a tiny specimen is placed 11 mm in front of the lens, what is the image distance?
options: 110 mm
100 mm
55 mm
220 mm

questions.question: A girl stands 4 m from a wall mirror. She then walks 1.5 m closer to the mirror. What is the new distance between her and her image?
options: 5 m
3 m
6 m
questions.explanation: Initial distance to mirror = 4 m. New distance to mirror = 4 - 1.5 = 2.5 m. Total distance to virtual image = 2 × 2.5 m = 5 m.

questions.question: A light ray travels from water (n = 1.33) into glass (n = 1.50) with an angle of incidence of 30°. What is the angle of refraction in the glass?
Why does the pitch of an ambulance siren appear higher as it approaches an observer and lower as it recedes?
options: Wavefronts are compressed ahead of the source and stretched behind it (Doppler effect)
The siren's internal motor rotates faster when the vehicle is moving
Sound travels faster through air in the direction of the moving car
Air friction absorbs low frequencies during the approach
questions.correct_answer: Wavefronts are compressed ahead of the source and stretched behind it (Doppler effect)
questions.explanation: The motion of the sound source compresses wavefronts ahead, increasing the frequency perceived by a stationary observer, and elongates them behind, lowering the perceived frequency.

questions.question: If a diverging lens is immersed in a liquid whose refractive index is GREATER than that of the lens material, how will the lens behave?
options: It will behave as a converging lens
It will become completely transparent and lose all refractive power
It will behave as an even stronger diverging lens
It will behave as a plane mirror
questions.correct_answer: It will behave as a converging lens
questions.explanation: By the Lens Maker's Formula 1/f = (n_lens/n_med - 1)(1/R1 - 1/R2), if n_med > n_lens, the term (n_lens/n_med - 1) changes sign, reversing the optical character from diverging to converging.

questions.question: A photographer covers the bottom half of a camera's convex lens with black opaque tape. How does this affect the photograph formed on the sensor?
options: The full image is still formed, but its brightness (intensity) is reduced by half
The top half of the photograph is completely cut off
The bottom half of the photograph is completely cut off
The photograph becomes completely blurry and unrecognizable
questions.correct_answer: The full image is still formed, but its brightness (intensity) is reduced by half
questions.explanation: Every section of a lens focuses light from the entire object onto the image plane. Covering half the aperture cuts incoming light flux by 50% without truncating the field of view.

questions.question: Why does sound travel faster on a hot summer afternoon than on a cold winter morning?
options: Acoustic speed in a gas is directly proportional to the square root of absolute temperature (v ∝ √T)
Hot air is denser than cold air, providing more particles per unit volume
Atmospheric pressure is always twice as high in summer
Sound frequency increases proportionally with ambient temperature
questions.correct_answer: Acoustic speed in a gas is directly proportional to the square root of absolute temperature (v ∝ √T)
questions.explanation: In gases, v = √(γRT/M). As absolute temperature T increases, the thermal root-mean-square speed of gas molecules rises, allowing faster transmission of vibrational acoustic pulses.

questions.question: How does an increase in air humidity affect the speed of sound propagation?
options: Speed increases because humid air is less dense than dry air at the same temperature and pressure
Speed decreases because water vapor makes air heavier and sluggish
Speed remains completely unaffected because humidity only alters wave frequency
Sound cannot travel in humid air due to acoustic absorption
questions.correct_answer: Speed increases because humid air is less dense than dry air at the same temperature and pressure
questions.explanation: Water vapor (molar mass ~18 g/mol) is lighter than diatomic nitrogen and oxygen (~29 g/mol). Adding moisture reduces the overall density ρ of air, increasing sound speed since v = √(γP/ρ).

questions.question: What happens to the critical angle of a glass-liquid boundary if the refractive index of the surrounding liquid is increased towards that of glass?
options: The critical angle increases towards 90°
The critical angle decreases towards 0°
The critical angle remains constant at 42°
Total internal reflection becomes impossible regardless of angle
questions.explanation: Since sin(θc) = n_liquid / n_glass, as n_liquid increases towards n_glass, the ratio approaches 1, meaning θc approaches arcsin(1) = 90°.

questions.question: Why does a concave mirror produce a sharp real image of a distant star at its principal focus, but a flat mirror cannot?
options: A concave mirror converges incoming parallel stellar rays to a common focal point
A flat mirror absorbs all light coming from stars
A flat mirror reflects light at angles greater than 90°
A concave mirror magnifies light waves by converting them to radio waves
questions.correct_answer: A concave mirror converges incoming parallel stellar rays to a common focal point
questions.explanation: Starlight arrives as parallel rays; a concave mirror's curvature directs all parallel incident rays through its focal point, concentrating light into a sharp real image.

questions.question: Why do stars twinkle when observed from the surface of Earth, whereas planets do not twinkle appreciably?
options: Stars are point sources whose rays deviate significantly through shifting atmospheric layers; planets are extended disks that average out fluctuations
Stars actively pulse in brightness, whereas planets reflect constant sunlight
Planets are closer than the atmosphere, so their light does not traverse air
Earth's magnetic field deflects starlight but not planetary light
questions.correct_answer: Stars are point sources whose rays deviate significantly through shifting atmospheric layers; planets are extended disks that average out fluctuations
questions.explanation: Atmospheric turbulence continually shifts the narrow beam from a point source (star). Extended disks of nearby planets act as numerous point sources whose random variations cancel out.

questions.question: When a sound wave reflects from a rigid wall back into the air, what phase change does the displacement wave undergo?
options: π radians (180°) phase reversal
Zero phase change
π/2 radians (90°) phase advance
2π radians phase shift
questions.explanation: Reflection of a mechanical displacement wave from a denser/rigid boundary results in a phase inversion of π radians (180°), creating a displacement node at the wall.

questions.question: Why is the core of an optical fiber manufactured with a higher refractive index than the surrounding cladding?
options: To satisfy the condition that light travels from a denser to a rarer medium for total internal reflection
To prevent electrical sparks from leaking out of the glass
To make the outer cladding more mechanically flexible
To absorb stray red photons and enhance blue signals
questions.correct_answer: To satisfy the condition that light travels from a denser to a rarer medium for total internal reflection
questions.explanation: TIR requires n_core > n_cladding so that light hitting the core-cladding interface at angles exceeding the critical angle is confined entirely within the core.

questions.question: What is the key functional difference between regular (specular) reflection and diffuse reflection?
options: Specular reflection reflects parallel rays in a single direction off smooth surfaces; diffuse scatters rays in all directions off rough surfaces
Specular reflection obeys the law of reflection, but diffuse reflection violates it
Diffuse reflection only happens with colored light
Specular reflection produces sound waves along with reflected light
questions.correct_answer: Specular reflection reflects parallel rays in a single direction off smooth surfaces; diffuse scatters rays in all directions off rough surfaces
questions.explanation: Both obey i = r at each local normal, but microscopic irregularities on a rough surface present normals in random directions, scattering parallel incident light diffusely.

questions.question: A person looks at their reflection in a large spherical mirror and finds their image is always upright and smaller regardless of how far they stand. What mirror is this?
options: Convex mirror
Concave mirror
Plane mirror
Parabolic concave mirror
questions.explanation: A convex mirror always forms a virtual, erect, and diminished image behind the mirror for all real object distances.

questions.question: In an experiment, red light and blue light are passed through the same glass prism. Which light ray undergoes greater deviation and why?
options: Blue light deviates more because glass has a higher refractive index for shorter wavelengths
Red light deviates more because red light has higher energy
Both deviate equally because angle of prism is constant
Red light deviates more because it travels faster in vacuum
questions.correct_answer: Blue light deviates more because glass has a higher refractive index for shorter wavelengths
questions.explanation: Due to optical dispersion, the refractive index of glass is higher for shorter wavelengths (n_blue > n_red). From δ ≈ (n - 1)A, blue light suffers a larger deviation.

questions.question: Why does the sun appear slightly oval or flattened near the horizon at sunrise and sunset?
options: Atmospheric refraction bends light from the lower edge of the solar disk more than from the upper edge
The sun physically compresses due to earth's gravitational pull
Hot air near the ground reflects the lower part of the sun
Dust particles in the horizon block light selectively
questions.correct_answer: Atmospheric refraction bends light from the lower edge of the solar disk more than from the upper edge
questions.explanation: Rays from the lower limb of the sun pass through denser air layers and refract upwards more strongly than rays from the upper limb, vertically compressing the apparent solar disk.

questions.question: In a reverberant empty auditorium, speech becomes indistinct and muddy. What acoustic phenomenon causes this issue?
options: Excessive reverberation due to repeated reflections from bare hard surfaces
Total absorption of high frequencies by the concrete floor
Destructive interference eliminating all sound waves
Doppler shifts created by stationary walls
questions.correct_answer: Excessive reverberation due to repeated reflections from bare hard surfaces
questions.explanation: Reverberation is the persistence of sound due to multiple diffuse reflections; if the reverberation time is too long, successive syllables overlap and garble speech.

questions.question: What is the optical reason behind the advance sunrise and delayed sunset by about 2 minutes each?
options: Atmospheric refraction bends sunlight around Earth's curvature
Light accelerates when traveling into Earth's gravitational field
Sunlight reflects off clouds in the upper stratosphere
Earth rotates slower at dusk and dawn
questions.correct_answer: Atmospheric refraction bends sunlight around Earth's curvature
questions.explanation: Earth's atmosphere bends sunlight downwards, allowing the sun to be seen when it is geometrically about 0.5° below the horizon, lengthening daylight by ~4 minutes daily.

questions.question: Why are two tuning forks of frequencies 256 Hz and 512 Hz sounded together perceived as an octave rather than discordant noise?
options: Their frequencies are in an exact 1:2 integer ratio, producing harmonious periodic beat patterns
Both tuning forks produce identical wavelengths in air
Their sound amplitudes cancel each other out completely
They share the exact same speed of sound
questions.correct_answer: Their frequencies are in an exact 1:2 integer ratio, producing harmonious periodic beat patterns
questions.explanation: A 2:1 frequency ratio represents an acoustic octave, where harmonics align perfectly without producing dissonant acoustic roughness.

questions.question: A ray of light enters a rectangular glass block at an angle of 45° and exits into air. What is the relationship between the incident ray and the emergent ray?
options: The emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray but laterally displaced
The emergent ray is perpendicular to the incident ray
The emergent ray converges towards the normal at 90°
The emergent ray is completely absorbed inside the block
questions.correct_answer: The emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray but laterally displaced
questions.explanation: Because opposite faces of a rectangular slab are parallel, the angle of emergence equals the angle of incidence (e = i), so the ray exits parallel but shifted sideways by lateral displacement.

questions.question: Why does a convex lens act as a burning glass when held in bright sunlight?
options: It converges parallel solar rays carrying thermal energy onto a tiny focal spot
The lens material generates heat through nuclear fusion
The glass amplifies the frequency of sunlight into infrared rays
It traps sunlight using total internal reflection
questions.correct_answer: It converges parallel solar rays carrying thermal energy onto a tiny focal spot
questions.explanation: Parallel rays from the sun converge at the principal focus of the convex lens, concentrating solar power per unit area sufficiently to ignite paper.

questions.question: Why can longitudinal waves travel through gases, liquids, and solids, whereas transverse mechanical waves propagate only through solids?
options: Transverse mechanical waves require shear elasticity, which fluids lack
Fluids cannot support volume compression
Longitudinal waves do not transmit mechanical energy
Particles in solids cannot oscillate back and forth
questions.correct_answer: Transverse mechanical waves require shear elasticity, which fluids lack
questions.explanation: Fluids yield continuously to shear stress and have no shear modulus, so shear (transverse) mechanical waves cannot propagate through the bulk of liquids or gases.

questions.question: How does wearing anti-reflective coating on eyeglasses reduce glare and improve clarity?
options: Destructive interference cancels light reflected from the front and back coating interfaces
The coating polarizes incoming light into ultrasound waves
The coating reflects 100% of visible light back outward
The coating absorbs all ultraviolet and visible light completely
questions.correct_answer: Destructive interference cancels light reflected from the front and back coating interfaces
questions.explanation: A coating of optical thickness λ/4 creates a path difference of λ/2 between reflections from its outer and inner boundaries, causing destructive interference that minimizes reflected glare.

questions.question: If a student wants to see an upright, enlarged image of their face using a mirror, which mirror and positioning should they choose?
options: Concave mirror with face placed inside the focal length (u < f)
Convex mirror with face placed at center of curvature (u = 2f)
Concave mirror with face placed beyond center of curvature (u > 2f)
Plane mirror placed 10 meters away
questions.correct_answer: Concave mirror with face placed inside the focal length (u < f)
questions.explanation: Only a concave mirror can produce a magnified virtual image, and it does so exclusively when the object is located between the pole and the principal focus (u < f).

questions.question: Why is ultrasound preferred over X-rays for monitoring fetal development during pregnancy?
options: Ultrasound uses non-ionizing mechanical sound waves that pose no radiation hazard to the fetus
Ultrasound produces higher resolution images of bone structures than X-rays
X-rays cannot penetrate amniotic fluid at all
Ultrasound destroys harmful bacteria in the womb
questions.correct_answer: Ultrasound uses non-ionizing mechanical sound waves that pose no radiation hazard to the fetus
questions.explanation: Ultrasound relies on high-frequency mechanical vibrations without ionizing radiation, making it completely safe for delicate fetal tissue compared to potentially mutagenic X-rays.

questions.question: In a physics lab, light passing through two different liquids A and B has critical angles 45° and 30° relative to air. Which liquid has a higher optical density?
options: Liquid B has a higher optical density because a smaller critical angle corresponds to a higher refractive index
Liquid A has a higher optical density because it has a larger critical angle
Both liquids have identical optical density
Optical density cannot be deduced from critical angles
questions.correct_answer: Liquid B has a higher optical density because a smaller critical angle corresponds to a higher refractive index
questions.explanation: Refractive index n = 1 / sin(θc). For A, n_A = 1/sin(45°) = 1.414; for B, n_B = 1/sin(30°) = 2.0. Higher refractive index means higher optical density.
